mode: Independent read-only official web documentation checks; no vendor account access or product trial.

sources.finding: Monthly Professional USD 35 and Enterprise USD 50 are present; the page labels its update date June 4, 2022. Current commercial confirmation remains required.

sources.locator: Customization, lookup fields and SalesInbox tables
sources.finding: Professional has custom modules and five lookup fields; Enterprise has multi-select lookup and SalesInbox. This supports the proposed configuration distinction without proving usability.

sources.locator: Plus and Pro monthly/annual price pairs
sources.finding: Monthly per-seat Plus USD 44 and Pro USD 99 support three-seat totals 132 and 297 before extras.
Custom objects require Pro or Enterprise.
Custom relationships require Pro or Enterprise; built-in relationships exist across all plans. A limitation on custom relationships does not mean no relationships at all.

sources.locator: Dependent modules and unsupported fields sections
sources.finding: Importer documentation supports dependent multi-select association files but excludes attachment fields from this import path.
This page still states multi-select lookup is unsupported for imported records. The conflicting documents justify an account-specific trial, not a definitive importer result.
Email content and attachments, Documents and integration-derived data are excluded. No complete-restoration test was performed.
Retrieved Growth card shows USD 39 per seat per month billed annually; three seats total USD 1404 yearly. This is not verified monthly-billing pricing.
A person has one native organization link and can have multiple deals; that alone does not establish an independent many-to-many location model.
The full export omits attached files, which the documentation directs users to download individually. UM commentary identifies a documented limitation, not an executed export result.

limitations: Official documentation describes capabilities; no configured-account behavior, quote, export completeness or assistant permission boundary was tested.
